originalPrompt:
Use case: design-decision web homepage comp.
Asset type: full fidelity landscape website homepage screenshot, 1536x1024, no browser chrome and no device frame.
Primary request: Design the new Birdcar operational consulting marketing homepage in a distinct "project folio" visual world. The website itself is organized like a beautifully clear working project folder. It is an actual designed homepage with readable navigation, headline, service explanation, action, and beginning of lower content, not a poster, photo, moodboard, logo sheet or picture of an office.
Input image: the supplied Alkaline typography specimen supplies the EXACT heavy connected italic signpainting letterforms for the Birdcar wordmark and the large headline. Use its letterforms only. Do not inherit the specimen composition. Use Barlow regular/medium for body and functional text.
Layout scaffold: landscape screen, a generous navy-on-white top navigation with Birdcar at left and "How it works", "Selected work", "Contact" at right. Below it one dominant asymmetric flat lilac folio spanning the page. The left 45 percent carries a monumental Alkaline headline on three deliberate lines "More room" / "to grow." and under it a clearly readable Barlow explanation, then a chartreuse primary button. The right 55 percent is a magnificent open assessment folio: two visible tabbed document layers, oversized clean report title, quiet structured observations and a diagram with only three simple boxes showing a workflow. It is one primary report object, not many floating small cards. Strong straight baselines, generous space, extreme clarity, a little confident overlap only at folder edges. Tiny clipped corners/tabs provide signature geometry, no ordinary rounded-card dashboard look. No generic browser-window frame around the document. The report lives in the page as a large designed document. A wide darker navy bottom fold carries three clearly spaced stages and begins the real project stories, sufficient to show this world continues below the hero. Whole page lit for an ordinary office/daylight reading scene, almost entirely flat.
Palette: precise midnight navy #142C3B text and grounding, lilac #C8B6F8 covering around 45 percent of the page, chartreuse #D3ED61 for the assessment action and active tab, cool near-white #F6F7F3 for report surfaces. Saturation is confident and contemporary, not dusty beige. No gradients, chrome gloss, glass, neon glows or distressed paper. Crisp printed color-block material, shallow physical overlap with very restrained separation shadows ONLY at overlapping report layers. All body copy high contrast.
Exact essential text: wordmark "Birdcar". Headline "More room to grow." Supporting copy "Custom systems for service businesses with too much chasing, copying and remembering." Button "Book a free assessment". Under button "A conversation. A practical report. Yours to keep." Report small label "Example assessment"; title "A clearer way to work"; tabs "Observe", "Plan", "Build"; three report headings "What gets stuck", "What could improve", "What happens next". A minimal illustrative workflow "Enquiry → Follow-up → Ready to start". Lower sequence "Understand the work" / "Build what helps" / "Keep it working". Below sequence the beginning of a simple two-column work index may show "DataDash / Craft & Communicate" and "Workshops / GHX".
Content truth: Birdcar serves owners and operations leads in established service businesses, roughly10–100 staff, especially DFW and surrounding states. Free assessment is a roughly one-hour conversation followed by a report they can take away. They can separately commission a build and ongoing care. No payment promises/prices, no invented testimonial, no business statistics, no unprovided client dashboard screenshot, no fabricated claims of client outcomes, no staff portrait. The report is a clearly labeled conceptual example, not a real client's confidential assessment. Make the promise and booking action immediately readable.
The visual form should make people feel the useful report is already within reach, and the practical relationship has a clear next step. Alkaline lettering brings human confidence to an exceptionally organized, vivid folio system. Main focal object the report plus large headline, supporting content calm. No literal birds or cars, no nostalgia desktop UI, no icons-only feature-card grid.
limitations: Generated type is an approximation; use actual bundled Alkaline and Barlow in implementation.
Example report is illustrative; client project rows are based on owner-provided facts.
